title: word2vec
text: Google's open-source tool turned words into lists of numbers that capture meaning. It became a standard building block for language AI.

title: Echo and Alexa
text: Amazon launched the Echo speaker with the Alexa voice assistant. It put a talking AI assistant into millions of homes.

title: TensorFlow
text: Google Brain open-sourced its machine-learning software. It gave researchers and companies free tools to build neural networks.

title: Tay
text: Microsoft's Twitter chatbot learned abuse from users and posted offensive tweets. Microsoft took it offline within a day.

title: PyTorch
text: Facebook's AI lab released PyTorch, a flexible deep-learning toolkit. It became the main tool for AI research.

title: GPT-1
text: OpenAI showed a model pre-trained on raw text could then be tuned for many tasks. It started the GPT line.

title: BERT
text: Google open-sourced BERT, a language model pre-trained on large amounts of text. It beat previous records on 11 language tasks.

title: GPT-2
text: OpenAI held back its full GPT-2 model, saying it could be misused for fake news. It released it in stages instead.

title: GPT-3
text: OpenAI's model, with 175 billion internal settings, learned new tasks from a few examples. OpenAI sold access to developers, not the model.

title: AlphaFold 2
text: DeepMind's AlphaFold 2 predicted protein shapes about as well as lab experiments at a scientific contest. Biologists called the problem largely solved.

title: DALL·E and CLIP
text: OpenAI showed DALL·E, which drew pictures from text descriptions, and CLIP, which matched images to words.

title: GitHub Copilot
text: GitHub, owned by Microsoft, previewed Copilot, which suggests code as you type. It ran on OpenAI's Codex model.

title: H100 chip
text: Nvidia announced the H100 'Hopper' chip. It became the most sought-after hardware for training large AI models.

title: PaLM
text: Google's PaLM had 540 billion internal settings and trained on 6,144 chips. It showed reasoning improving as models grew.

title: BLOOM
text: Over 1,000 researchers, coordinated by Hugging Face, released a 176-billion-setting model covering 46 languages. Anyone could download it.

title: Stable Diffusion
text: Stability AI released an image generator whose model files anyone could download. It ran on home computers and spread fast.

title: Character.AI beta
text: Ex-Google engineers Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas opened their chatbot site to the public. Users talk to AI characters.

title: ChatGPT
text: OpenAI released a free chatbot as a 'research preview'. It reached 100 million users in about two months.

title: Bard
text: Google announced its Bard chatbot, built on its LaMDA model, to answer ChatGPT. It opened first to trusted testers.

title: New Bing
text: Microsoft built OpenAI's model into Bing search. Satya Nadella said he wanted Google to 'show that they can dance'.

title: LLaMA
text: Meta shared its LLaMA model with researchers. The files leaked online within about a week, and other open models followed.

title: GPT-4
text: OpenAI's GPT-4 accepted images as well as text. It scored at human level on many professional and academic exams.

title: Claude
text: Anthropic, founded by former OpenAI staff, opened its Claude assistant to wider use. It came as Claude and the cheaper Claude Instant.

title: Pi
text: Inflection, led by DeepMind co-founder Mustafa Suleyman, launched Pi, a chatbot built for supportive personal conversation rather than work.

title: Llama 2
text: Meta released Llama 2 free for research and commercial use, with Microsoft as launch partner. Companies could now build products on it.

title: Mistral 7B
text: Paris start-up Mistral released its first model as a free torrent download. The licence allowed any use.

title: Grok
text: Elon Musk's xAI launched Grok, a chatbot with live access to posts on X. Musk pitched it against OpenAI.

title: Gemini 1.0
text: Google DeepMind launched Gemini in three sizes, built to handle text, images and sound together. It was Google's answer to GPT-4.

title: Sora
text: OpenAI previewed Sora, which made realistic video clips up to a minute long from a text prompt.

title: Claude 3
text: Anthropic's Claude 3 family came in three sizes: Haiku, Sonnet and Opus. Anthropic said Opus beat GPT-4 on several tests.

title: FSD v12
text: Tesla rolled out driving software run by one AI model trained on video. It replaced over 300,000 lines of hand-written code.

title: GPT-4o
text: OpenAI's GPT-4o handled text, sound and images in one model. It could hold a spoken conversation with little delay.

title: Llama 3.1 405B
text: Meta released a 405-billion-setting model it called the first frontier-level open model. Zuckerberg argued open source was the path forward.

title: o1
text: OpenAI's o1 was trained to 'think' step by step before answering. Other labs released reasoning models after it.

title: Hub passes 1 million models
text: Hugging Face's Hub, the main site for sharing AI models, passed one million public models.

title: Model Context Protocol
text: Anthropic published the Model Context Protocol, an open standard for linking AI assistants to outside tools and data. Rivals later adopted it.

title: Amazon Nova
text: Amazon launched Nova, its own AI models for text, images and video. Amazon was also Anthropic's largest investor.

title: DeepSeek-V3
text: Chinese lab DeepSeek released a downloadable model close to the best, with a reported $5.6 million final training run.

title: Humanity's Last Exam
text: Scale AI and the Center for AI Safety published Humanity's Last Exam, about 3,000 expert questions. Top models scored under 10%.

title: DeepSeek-R1
text: DeepSeek's free reasoning model rivalled OpenAI's o1. A week later Nvidia lost nearly $600 billion in market value in a day.

title: Grok 3
text: xAI launched Grok 3, trained on its Colossus supercomputer. Musk called it the 'smartest AI on Earth'.

title: Claude Code
text: Anthropic previewed Claude Code, a tool that reads, edits and tests code by itself from a developer's terminal.

title: Gemini 2.5 Pro
text: Google's Gemini 2.5 Pro, a model that reasons before answering, topped the LMArena leaderboard of user preferences.

title: Llama 4
text: Meta released Llama 4, open models built for text and images. A row over its leaderboard testing followed.

title: Claude 4
text: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4 and Sonnet 4, aimed at coding and long tasks. Claude Code became generally available.

title: Grok 4
text: xAI launched Grok 4 and a $300-a-month 'Heavy' tier. It came days after Grok posted antisemitic replies on X.

title: gpt-oss
text: OpenAI released gpt-oss, its first downloadable models since GPT-2 in 2019. The licence allowed commercial use.

title: GPT-5
text: OpenAI's GPT-5 put fast and reasoning models behind an automatic switch. Users objected, and OpenAI brought back GPT-4o within days.

title: MAI-1-preview
text: Microsoft AI, led by Mustafa Suleyman, unveiled MAI-1-preview, its first large model built fully in-house.

title: Tinker
text: Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab launched Tinker, its first product: a service for customising open models with your own data.

title: Gemini 3
text: Google's Gemini 3 led many tests on release. Sam Altman then declared a 'code red' at OpenAI.

title: Mistral 3
text: Mistral released its Mistral 3 family, topped by Large 3, as downloadable models free for any use.

title: Nemotron 3 Super
text: Nvidia released Nemotron 3 Super, a free 120-billion-setting model, and published its training data.

title: GPT-5.4
text: OpenAI's GPT-5.4 was its first general model able to operate a computer by reading the screen and using mouse and keyboard.

title: Claude Mythos Preview
text: Anthropic withheld Claude Mythos Preview because it could find and exploit software flaws. Selected partners used it to fix them.

title: Muse Spark
text: Meta Superintelligence Labs released Muse Spark, its first model, after Llama 4 disappointed. Unlike Llama, it launched closed.

title: GPT-5.5
text: GPT-5.5 was OpenAI's first newly pre-trained base model since GPT-4.5, aimed at long multi-step work. API prices doubled.

title: DeepSeek V4
text: DeepSeek previewed V4: a 1.6-trillion-setting Pro model and a smaller Flash model. Both could read about 750,000 words at once.

title: Gemini 3.5 and Omni
text: At Google I/O, Google released Gemini 3.5 Flash and Gemini Omni, which makes video from mixed inputs. Gemini 3.5 Pro was delayed.

title: Claude Fable 5
text: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5, a public version of Mythos with added safeguards. Mythos 5, without them, went only to vetted organisations.

title: Grok 4.5
text: xAI, now part of SpaceX, launched Grok 4.5 for coding and multi-step tasks. It was trained with Cursor, which SpaceX was buying.

title: Inkling
text: Thinking Machines released Inkling, its first model, as free-to-download files. The lab said it was not the strongest available.

title: Claude Opus 5
text: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 came close to Fable 5 on many tasks at about half the price.

title: GPT-6 Astra
text: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra was its first model rated 'Critical' for cyber-attack ability. Access began with vetted business customers.

title: Gemini 4 Argon
text: Google released Gemini 4 Argon, its most powerful model, to cyber-defence partners first. Public access had no date.

title: Mistral Large 4
text: Mistral previewed Large 4, a model with about one trillion settings. It promised free-to-download files by the end of October.

title: Muse Spark Open
text: Meta released Muse Spark Open as free-to-download files. It was Meta's return to open models after April's closed launch.
